correctness.rationale: For a chain, the source transfer map is the invertible bidiagonal map \(y_i=x_i-tx_{i-1}\). The standard order-simplex facet slacks telescope to one. After inverting the transfer, their Euclidean gradient norms are exactly the displayed \(N_j(t)\). Distance to facet \(j\) is therefore \(s_j/N_j(t)\); equalizing all facet distances and summing the slacks gives the exact unique inradius and incenter. Direct differentiation gives the two endpoint signs, so the inradius is strictly improved by moving into the interval from either endpoint. For \(m=2\), the denominator is a strictly convex symmetric function, proving the unique midpoint optimum.

value.rationale: The diagonal parameter is the canonical simultaneous path from the order polytope to the chain polytope inside the source's continuous hypercube family, rather than an arbitrary slice. The theorem gives its full Euclidean inball profile in every dimension and identifies a structural effect not visible from combinatorial or Ehrhart equivalence: every nontrivial chain becomes more inball-efficient at an interior parameter than at either classical endpoint. The explicit moving incenter and the closed midpoint optimum in dimension two provide exact quantitative geometry for a natural interpolation used to connect order- and chain-type degenerations.
